text:
maria: quick follow-up on the per-tenant memory lease RFC. i sketched a lightweight runtime contract where tenants request a lease (size + ttl) and the platform can revoke with a deadline/grace window. want to flush out callbacks and metrics before i write the RFC proper.

sam: sounds useful. is the goal more fairness or to give apps a chance to gracefully shed memory?

maria: both. fairness for bursts (noisy tenants) and graceful degradation for long-running sessions/pinned caches. hard evicting kills requests; soft revoke lets apps checkpoint or shrink caches.

alex: tradeoffs: 1) if we honor leases strictly we need overcommit accounting and admission control. 2) if revokes are advisory only, tenants may ignore and we end up forcing later which is worse UX.

jin: impl idea: grant "soft" leases plus a revocation token with a deadline. runtime keeps per-tenant ordered grant queue. when pressure happens we pick leases with earliest deadlines or lowest priority to revoke, issue callback.

tim: what about exposing an api: 
```
lease_id = runtime.request_lease(tenant_id, bytes, ttl_secs, priority=0)
// runtime will call tenant.on_reclaim(lease_id, target_bytes, reclaim_by_ts)
// tenant can respond with release_bytes or ack
```

this gives apps a clear contract.

maria: exactly. proposal: reclaim_by_ts = now + grace_window (e.g. 30s). runtime may also send a non-blocking recommendation earlier (e.g. shrink caches by X%). important to document that reclaim_by is a soft deadline; runtime may escalate to immediate reclaim if host is critically OOM.

sam: metrics we need: lease_requests, lease_grants, lease_revocations, percent_revoked_before_deadline, avg_reclaim_bytes, tenant_ignored_revokes. these map to SLOs we can warn on.

aj: (typo) alex: also need to think about quantization: small leases churn is bad. maybe only allow fixed granularity buckets (e.g. 16MB steps).

jin: plus allocation-level integration: allocators should tag allocations with lease_id so reclaim can walk per-tenant arenas instead of global scans. that reduces pause times.

maria: good point. allocator API sketch: `allocator.tag_allocation(ptr, size, lease_id)` and `allocator.iterate_and_free(lease_id, target_bytes)` — runtime calls the second when reclaiming.

tim: how does this behave on Dedicated vs Hosted? my take: Dedicated tenants get stronger lease guarantees (longer ttls, SLA) and Hosted defaults to advisory leases + immediate fallback to smaller models or queueing.

sam: security/abuse: a tenant could repeatedly request tiny leases to dodge eviction. we should rate-limit lease ops and require escalation for repeated denials.

maria: agree. also add a per-tenant nightly compaction window where ephemeral leases don't block defrag.

jin: edge case: CUDA pinned host buffers and stages — if reclaim asks for X bytes but all candidates are in GPU resident KV caches, we need a way to estimate reclaimable bytes without forcing full decode. maybe track reclaimable_by_type: {staging: bytes, kvcache: bytes, misc: bytes}. runtime should include that in the revoke message.

maria: good call. revoke payload: {lease_id, target_bytes, reclaim_by_ts, reclaimable_breakdown}. tenant can choose which to drop.

tim: ops-bot note: deploy canary for lease-metrics collector in cluster-3 scheduled tonight :deploy:

deploy-bot: canary started on cluster-3 for feature/lease-metrics, will forward logs to /observability/leases.

sam: next steps: maria to draft RFC with API sketches + metrics table. jin/alex to write allocator tagging PR. tim to update Hosted behavior doc. i'll add monitoring dashboards template.

maria: thanks all — i'll post the RFC draft by EOD and book a 30m sync early next week. :thumbsup:
